1 قَسَحَ , aor.
قَسَحَ , inf. n. قَسَاحَةٌ and قُسُوحَةٌ, It was, or became, hard, firm, or tough. (S, [in two copies belonging to me, but omitted in a third,] K.) ―
-b2- And قَسَحَ He twisted a rope. (K.) ＝
-A2- Also, aor. as above, inf. n. قُسُوحٌ, (TA,) and ↓ أَقسح (in some copies of the K ↓ اقتسح , TA,) He (a man) was much, or frequently, excited by vehement lust: (S, [in two copies belonging to me, but omitted in a third,] K:) or was excited by vehement lust. (TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
